_README: Accepted CodeQL security findings for the PRIVATE wachturm-source repo.
The private repo has no GitHub Advanced Security, so there is no Security
tab in which to triage and dismiss alerts. This file is that triage record,
in version control and reviewable in a diff.
Each entry suppresses a (rule, file) PAIR -- deliberately not the rule
globally. The same rule appearing in a NEW file still fails the build, so
this cannot silently absorb a future regression.
The public mirror (lernen-edu/wachturm) does not consult this file: it
uploads to Code Scanning and these are triaged in the Security tab there.
Line numbers are intentionally NOT recorded -- they churn on every edit.
Adding an entry requires a reason. If you cannot write one, fix the code.

reason: Wachturm is a sealed loopback lab. iris-nginx serves a self-signed
certificate and is reachable only on https://127.0.0.1:9000, so there
is no CA to validate against and no network path for a MITM. This is
the documented design -- see the open_iris_client docstring in
integrations/iris.py, which states it verbatim -- and the same call
already carries a `# noqa: S501` suppressing ruff's equivalent rule.
CodeQL is reporting the single deliberate `verify=False` on line 122
of iris.py, fanned out across every call site that reaches it.
Revisit if Wachturm ever talks to a non-loopback host: at that point
verification must be re-enabled rather than this entry widened.
`os.chmod(tmp, 0o644)` on a mkstemp file that is immediately
`docker cp`-ed into the portal container, which must be able to read
it. The content is lab progress state (scenario id, step status) --
no credentials or student PII -- and the file is unlinked right after
Weakest entry in this file: the window where it is world-readable in
/tmp is real, just low-value. Worth tightening to a 0700 parent dir
rather than a 0644 file if this code is touched again.
